t: The Austrians attacked first and by mid-afternoon had broken the French centre, and the French were withdrawing when Louis Desaix arrived with fresh troops at around 5:30 pm and the battle turned.

Austrian losses were about half the forces they had committed: 15 colours, 40 guns, almost 8,000 prisoners and 6,500 dead or wounded, against French casualties of about 4,700 killed and wounded and 900 missing or captured.
Bonaparte's army bulletin and three 'Official Reports' during his rule made the battle seem more planned and more impressive than it was, though participants described an army often close to defeat.
dyk: Napoleon is said to have been told by Desaix, who was killed that evening, 'This battle is completely lost. However, there is time to win another.'
ev: Bonaparte leads his Army of the Reserve over the Alps into Italy
The French seize Milan and cut the main Austrian supply route along the south bank of the Po
Genoa surrenders to the Austrians, freeing a large number of them for operations against the French
The Austrians attack across the Bormida and break the French centre by early afternoon
Desaix's arrival and Kellermann's cavalry charge turn the battle, and the Austrians are routed
Melas begins negotiations that lead to the Convention of Alessandria
Napoleon holds a ceremony on the field to lay the founding stone of a pyramid

f.place: On a plain east of Alessandria in Piedmont, northern Italy, between Marengo village, Castel Ceriolo and San Giuliano Vecchio, with the Fontanone stream between Marengo and the river Bormida
f.sides: France under the First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte, with the Army of the Reserve officially commanded by Louis Alexandre Berthier: 22,000 men and 15 guns at first, with 6,000 more when Desaix arrived. Austria under General Michael von Melas: 30,000 men and 100 guns
f.outcome: The Austrians, who had lost about half the forces they had committed, fell back into Alessandria. Within 24 hours Melas began negotiations that led to the Convention of Alessandria and the Austrian evacuation of north-western Italy west of the Ticino.
